name: Cuticle pusher

card.summary: Small manicure tool used to ease back the cuticle so nails look clean, even and longer.
card.note: Over-aggressive cuticle work can cause injury or infection.

quick.overview:
A cuticle pusher is a hand tool, commonly a small stick or spoon-shaped metal or wood tip, used in manicures to push back the cuticle at the base of the nail.

People use it for a neater nail bed and a clean outline around the nail, which can make nails look longer and better kept in photos and close contact.
quick.how: Used in manicure routines, often after softening the skin with water or cuticle oil, pushing gently along the nail base. Some people pair it with cuticle oil or nippers.
quick.risks: Pressing too hard can damage the nail matrix or skin. Unsterilised tools can introduce infection; public health guidance for pedicures flags higher risk for people with conditions such as diabetes.

lead: A cuticle pusher is a manicure and pedicure tool for moving the cuticle back from the nail plate, creating a clean line at the nail base.[1]

Neat cuticles are part of grooming: pushed-back skin exposes more nail, and a tidy edge looks groomed. The tool has no dedicated study base; related manicure and pedicure risks are described in general terms.[1]

chain: Push it back from the nail plate
angle.text: Pushing back the cuticle shows more of the nail and gives a tidier nail edge.

paras: The tool is used in manicures and pedicures to ease cuticle skin back from the nail. Wikipedia treats it under the broader pedicure topic and does not describe tool types in detail.[1]
General pedicure guidance notes that cuticle nippers can remove too much cuticle, that unsterilised instruments can transmit pathogens, and that people with diabetes face higher risk.[1]
